Keywords: Latin ports arms embargo and evasion
RagShortTexts: The council prohibited arms, iron, ship timber and pilotage to specified enemies.

Variants.Content: Lateran IV prescribed religious penalties for supplying arms, iron and ship timber to Saracens and for piloting their ships. Iron and timber had civil as well as military uses, so port operators faced questions about destinations and services. The prohibition affected trading choices, while seizure and punishment involved local authorities.

Port workers faced materials that could repair civilian craft or build warships, and pilotage was expressly included. An allegation required goods, destination and actual service, not religious identity as evidence.

Authorities enforcing an embargo needed to establish cargo, destination and participants and hear merchants’ explanations and objections. Suppliers, shipowners and pilots performed different acts. Seizing cargo also affected buyers, freight payments and debts, while port rivalry could give accusations a private motive.
